title: Why do 7, 11 and 13 bring back the three digit number?
description: A three digit number is written twice to make a six digit number, which is divided by seven, eleven and thirteen. Letters show the six digit number is the original times one thousand one, and one thousand one is seven times eleven times thirteen.
teaching_notes: One idea: repeating the digits multiplies the number by 1001, and 1001 is 7 times 11 times 13. Watch for students who see that the number comes back but cannot say why.

video_script.why: The child uses place value with letters for a three digit number and sees why the six digit number is the original times 1001.
video_script.substitution: Write abcabc as abc × 1000 + abc = abc × 1001, find 7 × 11 × 13 = 1001, and check with 254.
video_script.anchor: the number 254 written twice as 254254 on the board, to be divided by 7, 11 and 13
video_script.payoff_line: You get back the original three digit number
maths_rules: dividing abc × 1001 by 7, 11 and 13 in turn divides by 1001 and leaves abc
video_script.design: One idea: repeating the digits multiplies the number by 1001, and 1001 is 7 times 11 times 13. The six digit number stays on the board and the check is the last step.

beats.on_screen: a small title card From your book; 254 written twice as 254254; divide by 7, then 11, then 13

marks.book: the small title card From your book appears
marks.ask: the divisions by 7, 11 and 13 appear with a question mark

narration: <bookmark mark='book'/>This is a question from your book. Take any three digit number with digits eigh, bee and see.
<bookmark mark='repeat'/>Write the digits twice to make a six digit number. For example, two hundred fifty four becomes two hundred fifty four thousand two hundred fifty four.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>Divide by seven, then by eleven, then by thirteen. What do you get, and why?

beats.on_screen: the six digit number stays on the board while the child thinks

marks.think: Keeko sits at the corner of the board

beats.on_screen: 7 × 11 × 13 to be multiplied; abcabc to be written by place value

marks.plan: 7 × 11 × 13 and abcabc are shown side by side

narration: <bookmark mark='plan'/>The hint says to multiply seven, eleven and thirteen. We also need the six digit number by place value.

beats.on_screen: Given: a three digit number abc, written twice as abcabc

marks.given: abc and abcabc are written with letters

narration: <bookmark mark='given'/>Given, a three digit number with digits eigh, bee and see. It is written twice to make a six digit number.

beats.on_screen: To find: what we get after dividing by 7, 11 and 13 in turn

marks.find: the aim is written on the board

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to find what we get after dividing by seven, eleven and thirteen in turn.

marks.shift: the first abc slides three places to the left

beats.colours: the two copies of abc in two colours
narration: <bookmark mark='shift'/>Step one, shift the first copy up three places.
<bookmark mark='write'/>Eigh bee see written twice is eigh bee see times one thousand, plus eigh bee see.

marks.common: the common abc is pulled out in front

beats.colours: the common abc in the accent colour
narration: <bookmark mark='common'/>Step two, take out eigh bee see, because both parts have it.
<bookmark mark='write'/>The six digit number is eigh bee see times one thousand one.

marks.turn: the three divisions are joined into one division by 1001

narration: <bookmark mark='first'/>Step three, multiply seven, eleven and thirteen. Seven times eleven is seventy seven.
<bookmark mark='second'/>Seventy seven times thirteen is one thousand one.
<bookmark mark='turn'/>Dividing by all three, one after another, is dividing by one thousand one.
<bookmark mark='seven'/>Step four, check with two hundred fifty four. Dividing by seven gives thirty six thousand three hundred twenty two.
<bookmark mark='eleven'/>Dividing by eleven gives three thousand three hundred two.
<bookmark mark='thirteen'/>Dividing by thirteen gives two hundred fifty four.

beats.on_screen: Answer: result = abc, the original three digit number

marks.ans: the answer result = abc is boxed

narration: <bookmark mark='ans'/>You get back the original three digit number.
<bookmark mark='why'/>This works because the six digit number is eigh bee see times one thousand one. And one thousand one is seven times eleven times thirteen.
